meta.voice: Academic, slow, model-conscious, k-punk adjacent: the archive as an accounting device against computational euphoria.

landing_page.title: Insulindian Miracle
landing_page.dek: A stratified computational archive on city formation, institutional drift, and the resource curse, organized around 1,590,008 policy executions.
landing_page.lede: The old interface wanted the narcotic simplicity of a single large number. This one refuses it. The evidence base is now explicitly partitioned into a 1,000,008-execution legacy baseline sweep, a 90,000-execution canonical scenario suite, and a 500,000-execution stress cohort. The point is not scale as spectacle. The point is provenance: which cohort can speak, which cohort must stay silent, and which estimate is being smuggled across the border when the distinction is erased.

sections.title: Cohort Accounting Against The Big Number
sections.markdown:
The frontend now treats the evidence base as a stratified object:

$$N_{\mathrm{total}}=N_{\mathrm{legacy}}+N_{\mathrm{historical}}+N_{\mathrm{stress}}=1{,}000{,}008+90{,}000+500{,}000=1{,}590{,}008.$$

`legacy_1m` is broad baseline ranking. `historical_90k` is canonical scenario evidence. `stress_500k` is adversarial perturbation. A million rows no longer get to masquerade as a universal empirical settlement. The archive has learned to say: this number belongs here, and not there.

sections.title: A Peninsula Is A Prior
sections.markdown:
The model starts before policy. Terrain is not scenery; it is the prior distribution over possible urban futures. Candidate sites inherit accessibility, port access, river access, arability, defensibility, resource rent, and settlement suitability. Policy acts after that inheritance.

A reduced-form reward can be read as

$$r_{i,t}=G_i+\rho_{i,t}(\beta_0+\beta_1 e_{i,t})+\Gamma_{i,t}-K_{i,t},$$

where $G_i$ is durable geography, $\rho_{i,t}$ is remaining rent, $e_{i,t}$ is extraction, $\Gamma_{i,t}$ is agglomeration and network value, and $K_{i,t}$ is the congestion, depletion, and institutional damage the policy helps produce.

sections.title: Significance Is An Estimand
sections.markdown:
The archive does not perform statistical drama. Where policy draws are matched, it reports paired gaps,

$$\widehat{\Delta}_{\pi,\pi'}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{c=1}^{n}\left(R_{c,\pi}-R_{c,\pi'}\right),$$

with a 95 percent paired bootstrap interval. Where matching is absent or the cohort is not scenario-resolved, the claim is suppressed. This is boring in the right way. The interface now treats boredom as a defense against overclaiming.

sections.title: Policies Build Urban Form
sections.markdown:
The policy is not merely a selector. It is an urban planner under uncertainty. Concentrated exploitation produces different morphology from persistent forgetting or spatially informed allocation. The displayed diagnostics therefore include cumulative reward, oracle regret, final extraction, concentration, and rank-size slope:

$$\mathrm{HHI}=\sum_i s_i^2,\qquad \hat{\zeta}=\operatorname{slope}(\log \operatorname{rank}_i,\log \operatorname{population}_i).$$

A policy can win reward while building a brittle primate city. Another can leave reward on the table while preserving a polycentric system. The page is designed to keep that contradiction visible.

sections.title: Against Computational Totality
sections.markdown: The archive is slower now. It has less appetite for the ecstatic sentence in which a simulator becomes a world. Resource-curse theory, urban economics, and bandit regret are not fused into one proof; they are made to pass through the same machine, and the seams remain visible. That is the k-punk lesson in miniature: the system speaks most truthfully when it stops pretending its accounting has abolished history.

pull_quotes.quote: The big number remains, but it is no longer sovereign.
A cohort is not just metadata. It is the boundary of the claim.
The machine still runs; the interface now asks what, exactly, it has permission to say.

figure_captions.caption: The evidence program is partitioned into legacy baseline, historical scenario, and stress cohorts.
Policy ranking is shown as cohort-scoped evidence, not as an undifferentiated global verdict.
Reward, regret, extraction, concentration, and Zipf slope summarize the policy morphology of the current synthesis.
The archive exposes the arithmetic of its own authority.
Paired intervals are shown only for matched scenario-backed comparisons.
Raw trajectory traces remain interpretive evidence, not substitutes for cohort inference.
Resource rent and final population are deliberately kept separate; the resource curse lives in that non-identity.

baseline.title: Baseline: The Quiet Control
baseline.dek: Default peninsula dynamics: moderate resource rents, mild institutional drift, and no deliberate historical pathology.
baseline.lede: The baseline is not innocent. It is the control condition that makes the other scenarios legible: no boomtown lure, no primacy trap, no shock/reform rupture, no intensified resource curse. It asks what the allocation policies do when the peninsula is allowed to remain merely uneven rather than actively hostile.

sections.title: Control Regime
sections.markdown:
The baseline leaves the default reward machine intact. It therefore measures the ordinary interaction of geography, agglomeration, extraction drift, and reform. In notation, it is the reference environment $c_0$ against which the other scenario draws are interpreted:

$$\Delta_{\pi}(c)=R_{\pi}(c)-R_{\pi}(c_0).$$

The historical and stress cohorts use the baseline as a low-pathology anchor. The legacy million-run cohort remains useful for broad ranking, but it is not treated as scenario-specific proof.

sections.title: Reading The Chart
sections.markdown: If a policy performs well here and fails elsewhere, the failure is not generic incompetence; it is a reaction to a specific mechanism. That is why the baseline page is intentionally dull. Its dullness is the calibration device. The relevant question is not which algorithm is heroic under default conditions, but which algorithm collapses when the world stops being polite.

pull_quotes.quote: The baseline is the sound of the model before history intervenes.

resource-curse-scenario.title: Resource Curse: Rent As Institutional Weather
resource-curse-scenario.dek: A rentier-state scenario where resource reward and institutional damage move together.
resource-curse-scenario.lede: The scenario turns Sachs and Warner, Ross, and the conditional resource-curse literature into a reduced-form simulator. Resource abundance is not treated as a curse by metaphysics. It becomes dangerous when the institutional buffers around openness, capital, and reform are too weak to absorb the rent.

sections.title: Rent Mechanism
sections.markdown:
Resource-rich sites receive short-run reward through rent capture, but repeated investment raises extraction and depletes the institutional base. The causal cartoon is:

$$\rho_i \uparrow \Rightarrow r_{i,t}^{\mathrm{short}} \uparrow,\qquad e_{i,t+1}=e_{i,t}+f(\rho_i, a_{i,t})-b(o_{i,t},k_{i,t}).$$

Here $o_{i,t}$ is openness, $k_{i,t}$ is productive capital, and $b$ is the institutional buffer. The curse is the condition under which the first arrow overwhelms the second term.

sections.title: Cohort Reading
sections.markdown: Scenario claims come from `historical_90k` and `stress_500k`. The chart should be read as an interval-backed comparison of policies facing the same rent-biased draws. Forgetting policies are expected to abandon decaying rent arms earlier; spatial heuristics are expected to suffer when geography correlates with extraction rather than trade. This is not a macro estimate of any one country. It is a controlled degradation experiment.

pull_quotes.quote: The curse is not abundance. The curse is abundance under a weak buffer.

botswana.title: Botswana Exception: Resource Rent With Buffers
botswana.dek: The same rent problem under stronger institutional absorbers.
botswana.lede: This scenario is named for the exception logic in the resource-curse literature: rents do not mechanically destroy development when institutions convert windfall into durable public capacity. The model is still reduced-form, but the contrast is exact enough to matter.

sections.title: Buffered Rent
sections.markdown:
The operative difference from the curse scenario is not that resources disappear. It is that the buffers are stronger:

$$\frac{\partial e_{i,t+1}}{\partial \rho_i}\;\text{is damped by}\;o_{i,t}, k_{i,t}, a_{i,t}.$$

The scenario therefore tests whether policy differences shrink when the institutional landscape is self-correcting. If everything works here, that is not a refutation of policy design; it is evidence that the environment has made policy choice less decisive.

sections.title: Exception As Test
sections.markdown: The page should be read against `resource-curse-scenario`, not in isolation. The paired contrast asks whether the same simulator produces divergent futures when the resource channel is held conceptually constant and the institutional channel is moved. That is the academic point: resources are conditional, not destiny.

pull_quotes.quote: The exception is not outside the model; it is the model with the buffer turned back on.

open-cluster.title: Open Cluster: Trade Without Sovereignty
open-cluster.dek: A Hanseatic scenario where network position dominates extractive endowment.
open-cluster.lede: The open cluster treats trade as a spatial externality rather than a state command. It is a test of Krugman-style increasing returns and urban network effects under low resource salience.

sections.title: Network Reward
sections.markdown:
The relevant object is not a single city but a field of complementarities. A stylized network term is

$$\Gamma_{i,t}=\sum_{j\neq i}\exp(-d_{ij}/\lambda)\,P_{j,t}^{\alpha},$$

where $d_{ij}$ is site distance and $P_{j,t}$ is neighboring population. Policies that can read spatial structure should distribute investment across the cluster rather than chase one early mean.

sections.title: Polycentric Test
sections.markdown: The expected signature is not just reward. It is morphology: lower concentration, flatter primacy, and a rank-size distribution closer to a polycentric commercial system. The heatmap and histogram are there because reward alone would make the network illegible.

pull_quotes.quote: A trade league is not a city. It is a topology that happens to pay.

merchant-republic.title: Merchant Republic: The Port As Computation
merchant-republic.dek: A commercial-republic scenario where ports, capital, and accessibility become the reward surface.
merchant-republic.lede: The merchant republic is the archive's Dutch and Venetian thought-experiment: wealth from coordination, credible commitment, and port access rather than from extractive rent. It asks whether algorithms can distinguish commercial geography from resource geography.

sections.title: Commercial Geography
sections.markdown:
Trade-cluster sites receive openness and capital advantages. The reward field is therefore a geography of circulation:

$$r_{i,t}^{\mathrm{trade}}\approx G_i+\Gamma_{i,t}+\eta o_{i,t}k_{i,t}.$$

A spatial policy can become intelligent here for the same reason it can become dangerous in the resource curse: it trusts geography. The question is what geography encodes.

sections.title: Against The Primate City
sections.markdown: The academic analogue is not a megacity but a distributed commercial network. The scenario therefore punishes the lazy reading in which the best city must become the only city. Look to $\mathrm{HHI}$ and $\hat\zeta$ as much as reward; the merchant republic is a morphology test.

pull_quotes.quote: The same spatial trust that saves the port can damn the mine.

megacity-trap.title: Megacity Trap: Primacy As Exhaustion
megacity-trap.dek: An urban primacy scenario where one dominant site becomes a sink for institutional and spatial capacity.
megacity-trap.lede: The megacity trap encodes the Henderson problem: agglomeration is productive until congestion, overstretch, and political centralization turn scale into drag. The model does not moralize size. It asks when size stops paying.

sections.title: Overstretch
sections.markdown:
The scenario increases the penalty for excessive concentration. If $s_i$ is the population share of the leading site, the relevant diagnostic is

$$\mathrm{HHI}=\sum_i s_i^2,$$

with the model imposing additional drag when primacy crosses the configured threshold. The policy problem is no longer only finding the best site; it is refusing to let the best site consume the system.

sections.title: Urban Form
sections.markdown: A high reward with a high concentration signature is not an unambiguous success here. The scenario exists because a city system can optimize the present by damaging its future option set. The page's cohort charts should therefore be read as reward plus morphology, not reward alone.

pull_quotes.quote: The megacity is the victory condition that becomes a trap.

balanced-urban.title: Balanced Urban System: Polycentric Carrots
balanced-urban.dek: A secondary-city scenario where the reward landscape explicitly favors distributed development.
balanced-urban.lede: Balanced urbanism is the scenario of intentional anti-primacy. It encodes the intuition that a system of secondary cities can carry resilience, specialization, and lower congestion without requiring one capital to swallow the whole future.

sections.title: Secondary City Bonus
sections.markdown:
The reward surface contains a deliberate midsize-city term. In reduced form:

$$B(P_i)=b\exp\left[-\frac{(P_i-P^*)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right],$$

so a site can be too small to coordinate and too large to remain efficient. This is an urban economics test, not a generic diversification slogan.

sections.title: Two Intelligences
sections.markdown: Spatial methods can win by recognizing the distributed reward surface. Forgetting methods can win by noticing when marginal returns decline and moving on. If both converge on polycentricity, that is not redundancy; it is two different algorithms discovering the same urban form.

pull_quotes.quote: Polycentricity is not indecision. It is a different objective function.

shock-reform.title: Shock Reform: Crisis As An Update Operator
shock-reform.dek: A crisis scenario where institutional rupture can damage a site and then make it newly viable.
shock-reform.lede: The shock-reform scenario is a reduced-form version of the political economy of crisis: reforms often arrive after the old equilibrium becomes unsustainable. The bandit problem is that the same site can be correctly abandoned and later correctly revisited.

sections.title: State Change
sections.markdown:
A shock changes the transition law. The planner is no longer estimating a stationary arm:

$$P(x_{t+1}\mid x_t,a_t,\mathrm{shock}=1)\neq P(x_{t+1}\mid x_t,a_t,\mathrm{shock}=0).$$

This is why a one-step oracle is not a dynamic god. It can see the current reward surface but not a full reform trajectory.

sections.title: Memory And Return
sections.markdown: Forgetting can be intelligence when the world has genuinely changed. Too much memory treats the post-shock site as the pre-shock site forever. Too little memory chases noise. The cohort comparison is therefore a test of temporal calibration: how fast can a policy revise without becoming pure amnesia?

pull_quotes.quote: The crisis is not the lesson. The update is.

ucb-bait.title: UCB Bait: The Boomtown That Was Partly Real
ucb-bait.dek: A boom-bust trap where early reward is genuine enough to poison the estimate.
ucb-bait.lede: The trap is not that the boomtown is fake. It is worse than that. It is briefly true. An optimistic average can therefore learn the wrong lesson with statistical confidence, exactly when a decaying arm is converting reward into future damage.

sections.title: Bait Mechanism
sections.markdown:
The scenario adds a strong early boomtown bonus and then accelerates collapse. For an optimistic average, the estimated arm value can remain high after the latent process has turned:

$$\hat\mu_{i,t}=\frac{1}{n_i}\sum_{\tau:a_\tau=i}r_{i,\tau},\qquad r_{i,t+k}<r_{i,t}\;\text{after collapse}.$$

That lag is the bait. The confidence term narrows around a mean contaminated by the past.

sections.title: Exit Plan
sections.markdown: The stress cohort overweights this regime because it is where nonstationarity stops being decorative and becomes lethal. The policy question is not whether to exploit the boom. It is whether the policy can take the opening rent without becoming the institution that the rent destroys.

pull_quotes.quote: The boomtown is not false. It is temporarily true, and that is why it works.

bibliography_annotations.lattimore2020bandit: The formal backbone for regret, policy interfaces, and the discipline that keeps the archive from becoming metaphor.
bibliography_annotations.russo2018thompson: The best compact account of posterior sampling as calibrated uncertainty rather than decorative randomness.
bibliography_annotations.auer2002ucb1: The clean stationary optimism baseline; useful here because its misspecification is visible.
bibliography_annotations.whittle1988restless: The conceptual source for restless allocation, with the usual warning that the implementation is a surrogate heuristic.
bibliography_annotations.akbarzadeh2020whittle: A technical anchor for indexability and Whittle-style computation, used as a caution as much as a guide.
bibliography_annotations.levine2017rotting: Names the core decay problem directly: arms can worsen under use.
bibliography_annotations.henderson1974cities: The agglomeration-versus-congestion frame behind primacy, secondary cities, and urban system size.
bibliography_annotations.krugman1991geography: Increasing returns and spatial concentration, translated here into accessibility and network rewards.
bibliography_annotations.sachs1995resourcegrowth: The empirical resource-curse anchor whose reduced-form logic becomes extraction drift.
bibliography_annotations.ross1999resourcecurse: Rentier-state and elite-capture mechanisms behind the institutional interpretation of resource rewards.
bibliography_annotations.acemoglu2001colonial: Institutional starting conditions and path dependence, used here as motivation rather than causal identification.
